summary: San Juan Bautista occupies less than a single square mile yet holds one of California's original 21 Spanish missions — Mission San Juan Bautista, founded in 1797, which still anchors a remarkably intact historic plaza that Alfred Hitchcock used as a filming location for *Vertigo*. That plaza, lined with adobe structures and a small cluster of restaurants and shops along Third Street, essentially *is* the town center, giving the place a density of character that belies its population of roughly 2,100. The setting is the San Juan Valley at the western edge of the San Benito County agricultural corridor, with the Gabilan Range rising to the east and the San Andreas Fault literally running through the edge of town — visible as a subtle escarpment near the mission. The economy here is not self-contained: with virtually no major employers within city limits, most working residents commute — Hollister is seven miles south, and Gilroy and its US-101 corridor sit about fifteen minutes north, connecting to Silicon Valley jobs roughly an hour away. A median home value around $707,100 against a median household income near $108,750 produces a price-to-income ratio above 6.5, steep but noticeably below neighboring Santa Cruz or Santa Clara counties. Evenings are genuinely quiet — no nightlife infrastructure to speak of, though the mild year-round climate (averaging 69°F days with nine hours of sunshine) makes the surrounding open hillsides and the Flint Hills area walkable most of the year. The tradeoff is stark: you get a town with an almost unreasonably photogenic historic core and gentle inland-California weather, but you drive for nearly everything — groceries, healthcare, varied dining, employment.
